fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can locate the property quickly from the street.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the opening, particularly if vegetation narrows the approach.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Maintain a minimum vertical clearance along the entire driveway length so larger emergency vehicles, including fire apparatus, can travel without overhead branches blocking passage.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence or detached structure large enough for an emergency vehicle to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so it remains available when responders arrive.
• Post a simple map or diagram at the road entrance showing the driveway route, the location of the main residence, and the location of the detached structure.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain clear sightlines for responders moving between the road and the structures.
• Keep a clear path on foot between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without pushing through dense growth.
• Mark or identify the detached structure from the driveway so arriving responders can see it without searching the property.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin trees in the clusters nearest to the structure to create open gaps between the tree canopies.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Clear a wider band of low shrubs and ground-level plants from around the entire structure perimeter.
• Separate shrub groupings from nearby tree clusters so vegetation does not form a continuous path to the structure.
• Cut back or remove shrubs and low branches along both sides of the driveway for its full length.
• Trim overhanging tree branches along the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, debris, and encroaching vegetation.
• Maintain a wide enough cleared area along the driveway so two vehicles can pass or a large vehicle can turn around.
• Thin scattered trees on the approach side of the property so the driveway remains visible and accessible from the road.
• Remove dead wood, fallen branches, and accumulated leaf litter from the ground around the structure.
• Keep the area directly under trees near the structure free of shrubs and ground cover that could carry fire up into the tree canopy.
